Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 03-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - JANUARY 2026  
  Computer Vision [IT_4408]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                 Modern industries and intelligent systems increasingly rely on computer vision for automation and        (5)  
  decision-making.  
  A)            Discuss one real-world application (for example: autonomous driving, medical diagnosis, or  
  industrial inspection)  
  and Discuss how computer vision transforms raw images into meaningful actions or insights  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)            Computer Vision plays a vital role in sports analytics - from tracking player movement to detecting      (5)  
  ball trajectories. Analyse how Computer Vision enables such applications with a step-by-step  
  approach  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                 Illustrate how edge detection techniques help in obtaining important structural details from digital     (5)  
  images. Compare the working principles of the Laplacian and Canny edge detection methods  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Apply bit slicing, on the 4*4 matrix of your choice. Discuss the concept of bit slicing in detail. Write (5)  
  each pixel in 4-bit binary and give the bit-plane b3 (MSB) and bit-plane b0 (LSB) as binary matrices  
  (0/1).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                 A self-driving car uses multiple cameras mounted at different angles. Apply your understanding of        (5)  
  different camera models to explain how various camera models account for the differences in the  
  A)            field of view and distortion.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)            Analyse translation, rotation, and scaling operations to register two medical images of the same         (5)  
  patient taken at different time intervals.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                 Analyze the Lucas-Kanade optical flow (point-based) to compute vehicle lane changes from                 (5)  
  dashcam video. Formulate how tracked points on lane markings are used to infer lateral vehicle  
  A)            motion and determine lane-change events.  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Apply the mean-shift algorithm for real-time tracking of colored buoys in a marine robotics           (5)  
  application. Explain how you would choose the kernel bandwidth, color space, and target model to  
  be robust to lighting changes and reflections.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                        Analyze face recognition algorithms to design a secure office entry system that identifies authorized (5)  
  personnel. Explain how training data and distance thresholds affect system reliability.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                Apply the BoW technique to categorize sports scenes (e.g., soccer, swimming, basketball) from   (5)  
  video frames. Discuss how you would combine spatial pyramids or temporal information to enhance  
  recognition accuracy  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
